project.title: Research on agricultural and forestry waste-based deodorizing fillers for rural domestic sewage treatment facilities and their application
project.description: Decentralized rural wastewater treatment in China is plagued by ammonia-rich malodor due to inadequate O&M. Conventional media are costly with poor microbial affinity, while agricultural waste alternatives lack mechanistic clarity and scale-up validation. This study evaluates loofah sponge and pine bark against an activated carbon-ceramsite control. Integrated multifactorial tests, microbial sequencing, and field trials reveal that pine bark offers superior shock load resistance and temperature adaptability, maintaining 97%-99% ammonia removal at 70-90 L/min and <=70 ppm inlet concentrations. The optimized pine bark-ceramsite composite forms a hierarchical porous structure with sustained lignocellulose-driven nutrient release, boosting the key nitrifier Nitrospira to 19.25% abundance and establishing a resilient ammonia-degrading microecosystem. Loofah sponge, despite high porosity, suits only low-load, temperature-controlled scenarios. Engineering application confirms the composite slashes deodorization costs to CNY 92.14 per ton of wastewater, with effluent meeting national standards. This work deciphers the structure-activity relationship of biomass-based fillers, providing a cost-effective, eco-friendly paradigm for scaling odor mitigation in decentralized rural infrastructure.
